newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin may loosen embrace on Love Parade.
newsitem.headline: Berlin may loosen embrace on Love Parade.

text.p: The Love Parade, a giant techno party expected to attract a million young people from around the world to Berlin on July 12, may be moved to other cities in future, organisers said on Thursday.
"There is consideration being discussed of staging a European-wide Love Parade and not having it in Berlin any more," said Parade director Ralf Regitz.
The annual event has grown into a massive spectacle since it was launched in Berlin in 1989 with only a few hundred participants.

More than a million people are expected to gyrate down the streets of the German capital on July 12 for the eighth annual "Love Parade", a six-km (four-mile) long "rave" of electronic music and dancing.
Regitz said the ravers of the future could be diverted to other European cities such as Vienna and Zurich.

The parade has run into steamy opposition from nature lovers and some city authorities who object to the noise, mountains of garbage and outlawed substances brought to the city every year by raucous music lovers.
But the hotel and tourism industry have become ardent supporters of the event, which added an estimated 110 million marks ($64 million) to Berlin's economy last year.

The BUND environmental group tried unsuccessfully to block this year's parade with a court injunction saying party-goers were likely to damage the city's historic Tiergarten park, which runs along the parade route.
